title: Q-SUBST-red-pr-latency: repair a red pull request within one hour, not at the next executor slot
body:
**Owner:** operations
**Trigger:** SUBSTANCE-1 audit 2026-11-21
**Done check:** cmd:python3 -m foundation lanewatch --check
**Status:** closed

SUBSTANCE-1 audit, 2026-11-21: PR 826 (DISCOVER-1) failed checks at 20:39 UTC and merged at 07:29 the next day. The lane filed OL-PR-826 and commented five times in four minutes (fixed: LANE-DEDUPE-1 in foundation/loopowner.py), but the repair waited for the executor, whose runs are capped per day (doctrine/clocks.json chain.max_runs_per_day) with its daily cron at 06:23. Remedy: when the lane files an OL-PR item for a ci-failed PR, dispatch the executor for that item at once (bounded by the Actions budget guard), and measure red-to-merged hours in the lane's own evidence.

**Vacuous:** 2026-11-21T11:20:52Z vacuous: the probe was never recorded failing on this item, so its pass cannot show the defect is gone; rewrite the probe so it fails while the defect exists


**Evidence:** closing probe passed (2 consecutive passes after a recorded failure): lanewatch ok


**Relapse:** 2026-11-25T12:01:26Z closing probe failed again: lanewatch: PR #2080 is green and unmerged after 829 min: the lane has not merged it; run the lane (scripts/lane.sh)
lanewatch: 1 green PR(s) not merged (reopen 1; closes again only after 2 passes over 60 minutes)

**Disposition:** shelved (ttl, 2026-11-25T12:02:31Z, DISPOSE-1)

**Evidence:** open 96.9 hours (limit 6 hours) and no loop closed it (SLA-8H-1). Its closing probe still runs on every fleet pass and records `fixed` when it passes; the executor retries it when its open queue is empty (every 30 days at most).
